# Made by `python3 -I tools/reference.py shell-table` from docs/reference/*.txt. Do not edit.
== string
syn: string SUBCOMMAND ?ARG ...?
sub: string length STRING | Gives the count of characters of a string.
sub: string length -grapheme STRING | Counts grapheme clusters in place of characters.
sub: string bytelength STRING | Gives the count of bytes of the UTF-8 form of a string.
sub: string insert STRING INDEX TEXT | Gives a string with text put before the character at an index.
sub: string index STRING INDEX | Gives the character at an index of a string.
sub: string index -grapheme STRING INDEX | Counts INDEX in grapheme clusters, and gives a whole cluster.
sub: string range STRING FIRST LAST | Gives the characters of a string from one index to another.
sub: string range -grapheme STRING FIRST LAST | Counts FIRST and LAST in grapheme clusters.
sub: string first NEEDLE HAYSTACK ?START? | Gives the index of the first match of a substring.
sub: string last NEEDLE HAYSTACK ?LAST? | Gives the index of the last match of a substring.
sub: string compare ?-nocase? ?-length N? A B | Compares two strings character by character.
sub: string equal ?-nocase? ?-length N? A B | Tests whether two strings are the same text.
sub: string match ?-nocase? PATTERN STRING | Tests whether a glob pattern matches the whole of a string.
sub: string map ?-nocase? MAPPING STRING | Replaces each key of a list of keys and values with its value.
sub: string repeat STRING COUNT | Gives a string repeated a number of times.
sub: string replace STRING FIRST LAST ?NEW? | Gives a string with a range of characters replaced by other text.
sub: string reverse STRING | Gives the characters of a string in the reverse order.
sub: string reverse -grapheme STRING | Reverses the order of the grapheme clusters, each with its characters in order.
sub: string tolower STRING ?FIRST? ?LAST? | Gives a string with its letters in lowercase.
sub: string toupper STRING ?FIRST? ?LAST? | Gives a string with its letters in uppercase.
sub: string totitle STRING ?FIRST? ?LAST? | Gives a string with its first character in title case and the rest in lowercase.
sub: string trim STRING ?CHARS? | Gives a string with given characters removed at both ends.
sub: string trimleft STRING ?CHARS? | Gives a string with given characters removed at the start.
sub: string trimright STRING ?CHARS? | Gives a string with given characters removed at the end.
sub: string is CLASS ?-strict? ?-failindex VAR? STRING | Tests whether a string is of a class, such as integer or alpha.
sub: string cat ?STRING ...? | Joins strings with no separator.
sub: string wordstart STRING INDEX | Gives the index of the first character of the word at an index.
sub: string wordend STRING INDEX | Gives the index after the last character of the word at an index.
== tcl::prefix
syn: tcl::prefix subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: tcl::prefix match ?-exact? ?-message TEXT? ?-error OPTIONS? TABLE STRING | The entry of TABLE that STRING is a unique prefix of, or an error.
sub: tcl::prefix all TABLE STRING | Each entry that starts with STRING.
sub: tcl::prefix longest TABLE STRING | The longest common prefix of those entries.
== append
syn: append varName ?value ...?
== concat
syn: concat ?arg ...?
== format
syn: format formatString ?arg ...?
== scan
syn: scan string format ?varName ...?
== split
syn: split string ?splitChars?
syn: split string splitChars -grapheme
== join
syn: join list ?joinString?
== regexp
syn: regexp ?-option ...? exp string ?matchVar? ?subMatchVar ...?
opt: -nocase | Matches letters with no case.
opt: -all | Finds each match.
opt: -inline | Gives the match and its groups as a list, and sets no variable.
opt: -indices | Gives the start and end index of each match in place of the text.
opt: -start INDEX | Starts the search at INDEX.
opt: -line | ^ and $ match at each line, and .
opt: -expanded | White space and # comments in exp are ignored.
opt: -about | Gives the count of groups and the flags of exp.
== regsub
syn: regsub ?-option ...? exp string subSpec ?varName?
opt: -all | Replaces each match.
opt: -nocase | Matches letters with no case.
opt: -start INDEX | Starts the search at INDEX.
== subst
syn: subst ?-nobackslashes? ?-nocommands? ?-novariables? string
== encoding
syn: encoding option ?arg ...?
sub: encoding convertto ?-profile PROFILE? ?-failindex VAR? ENCODING STRING | The bytes of STRING in ENCODING, as a byte string.
sub: encoding convertfrom ?-profile PROFILE? ?-failindex VAR? ENCODING BYTES | The text of BYTES in ENCODING.
sub: encoding profiles | The profiles: replace strict tcl8.
sub: encoding user | The encoding of the user: utf-8.
sub: encoding names | The names of the encodings: the ones with no table, and the files of the encoding folders.
sub: encoding system | The encoding of the system: utf-8.
sub: encoding dirs ?LIST? | The folders of the encoding files of Tcl (koi8-r.enc, iso2022-jp.enc, ...).
== binary
syn: binary subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: binary format TEMPLATE ?VALUE ...? | Gives the bytes.
sub: binary scan BYTES TEMPLATE ?VAR ...? | Sets the variables and gives the count of values that it read.
sub: binary encode FORMAT ?-option value ...? DATA | base64, hex, or uuencode text of the bytes.
sub: binary decode FORMAT ?-option value ...? DATA | The bytes of the text.

syn: lreplace LIST FIRST LAST ?ELEMENT ...?
== lreverse
syn: lreverse LIST
== lsearch
syn: lsearch ?OPTION ...? LIST PATTERN
opt: -glob | Matches PATTERN as a glob pattern; the default.
opt: -exact | Matches an element that equals PATTERN.
opt: -regexp | Matches PATTERN as a regular expression.
opt: -sorted | Searches a sorted list with a binary search.
opt: -bisect | Gives the index of the last element at or before PATTERN in a sorted list.
opt: -all | Gives each match in place of the first one.
opt: -inline | Gives the matching elements in place of their indexes.
opt: -not | Finds the elements that do not match.
opt: -start INDEX | Starts the search at an index.
opt: -ascii | Compares the elements as text; the default type.
opt: -dictionary | Compares the elements in dictionary order.
opt: -integer | Compares the elements as integers.
opt: -real | Compares the elements as floating-point numbers.
opt: -nocase | Matches letters with no regard to case.
opt: -increasing | Says that a sorted list is in increasing order; the default.
opt: -decreasing | Says that a sorted list is in decreasing order.
opt: -index INDEX | Compares an element of each element in place of the whole element.
opt: -subindices | With -index, gives the path of the match or the subelement.
opt: -stride N | Reads the list as groups of N elements.
== lseq
syn: lseq COUNT
syn: lseq START ?to|..? END ??by? STEP?
syn: lseq START count COUNT ??by? STEP?
== lset
syn: lset VAR ?INDEX ...? VALUE
== lsort
syn: lsort ?OPTION ...? LIST
opt: -ascii | Compares the elements as text; the default type.
opt: -dictionary | Compares the elements in dictionary order: no case, and runs of digits as numbers.
opt: -integer | Compares the elements as integers.
opt: -real | Compares the elements as floating-point numbers.
opt: -command SCRIPT | Compares two elements with a command.
opt: -increasing | Sorts from the smallest element to the largest; the default.
opt: -decreasing | Sorts from the largest element to the smallest.
opt: -nocase | Compares the text with no regard to case.
opt: -unique | Keeps one element of each group of equal elements.
opt: -indices | Gives the indexes of the elements in sorted order.
opt: -index INDEX | Compares an element of each element in place of the whole element.
opt: -stride N | Sorts groups of N elements.
== dict
syn: dict SUBCOMMAND ?ARG ...?
sub: dict create ?KEY VALUE ...? | Makes a dict from keys and values.
sub: dict get DICT ?KEY ...? | Gives the value at a path of keys.
sub: dict getdef DICT ?KEY ...? KEY DEFAULT | Gives the value at a path of keys, or a default when a key is missing.
sub: dict getwithdefault DICT ?KEY ...? KEY DEFAULT | Gives the value at a path of keys, or a default: the same command as dict getdef.
sub: dict exists DICT KEY ?KEY ...? | Tests whether a path of keys exists.
sub: dict set VAR KEY ?KEY ...? VALUE | Sets the value at a path of keys in the dict of a variable.
sub: dict unset VAR KEY ?KEY ...? | Removes the key at the end of a path from the dict of a variable.
sub: dict keys DICT ?PATTERN? | Gives the keys of a dict, or the keys that match a glob pattern.
sub: dict values DICT ?PATTERN? | Gives the values of a dict, or the values that match a glob pattern.
sub: dict size DICT | Gives the count of keys of a dict.
sub: dict for {KEYVAR VALUEVAR} DICT BODY | Runs a script for each key and value of a dict.
sub: dict map {KEYVAR VALUEVAR} DICT BODY | Makes a dict with the same keys and the results of a script as values.
sub: dict filter DICT key ?PATTERN ...? | Gives the keys and values of a dict that pass a test.
sub: dict filter DICT value ?PATTERN ...? | Gives the keys and values of a dict that pass a test.
sub: dict filter DICT script {KEYVAR VALUEVAR} BODY | Gives the keys and values of a dict that pass a test.
sub: dict merge ?DICT ...? | Joins dicts into one, with the value of a later dict for a key in both.
sub: dict remove DICT ?KEY ...? | Gives a copy of a dict with some keys removed.
sub: dict replace DICT ?KEY VALUE ...? | Gives a copy of a dict with new values for some keys.
sub: dict incr VAR KEY ?INCREMENT? | Adds an integer to the value of a key in the dict of a variable.
sub: dict append VAR KEY ?STRING ...? | Adds text to the end of the value of a key in the dict of a variable.
sub: dict lappend VAR KEY ?VALUE ...? | Adds elements to the list value of a key in the dict of a variable.
sub: dict update VAR KEY VARNAME ?KEY VARNAME ...? BODY | Runs a script with variables linked to keys of the dict of a variable.
sub: dict with VAR ?KEY ...? BODY | Runs a script with a variable for each key of the dict of a variable.
sub: dict info DICT | Gives text for people with the count of entries of a dict.
== array
syn: array subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: array set NAME LIST | Sets the elements from a list of names and values.
sub: array get NAME ?PATTERN? | A list of names and values.
sub: array names NAME ?MODE? ?PATTERN? | The element names.
sub: array exists NAME | 1 when the variable is an array.
sub: array for {KEYVAR VALUEVAR} NAME BODY | Runs BODY once for each element of a copy of the array.
sub: array default get|set|exists|unset NAME ?VALUE? | The value that a read of a missing element gives.
sub: array size NAME | The count of elements.
sub: array unset NAME ?PATTERN? | Removes the elements, or the whole array.
sub: array statistics NAME | Text about the hash table.
sub: array startsearch NAME | A search id, for the old way to go through an array one element at a time.
sub: array nextelement NAME ID | The next element name of the search.
sub: array anymore NAME ID | 1 when the search has more elements.
sub: array donesearch NAME ID | Ends the search.

syn: expr ARG ?ARG ...?

== tcl::mathfunc tcl::mathfunc::abs tcl::mathfunc::acos tcl::mathfunc::asin tcl::mathfunc::atan tcl::mathfunc::atan2 tcl::mathfunc::bool tcl::mathfunc::ceil tcl::mathfunc::cos tcl::mathfunc::cosh tcl::mathfunc::double tcl::mathfunc::entier tcl::mathfunc::exp tcl::mathfunc::floor tcl::mathfunc::fmod tcl::mathfunc::hypot tcl::mathfunc::int tcl::mathfunc::isqrt tcl::mathfunc::log tcl::mathfunc::log10 tcl::mathfunc::max tcl::mathfunc::min tcl::mathfunc::pow tcl::mathfunc::rand tcl::mathfunc::round tcl::mathfunc::sin tcl::mathfunc::sinh tcl::mathfunc::sqrt tcl::mathfunc::srand tcl::mathfunc::tan tcl::mathfunc::tanh tcl::mathfunc::wide

syn: upvar ?level? otherVar localVar ?otherVar localVar ...?
== trace
syn: trace option ?arg ...?
sub: trace add variable NAME OPS CMD | OPS is a list of read, write, unset, and array.
sub: trace add command NAME OPS CMD | OPS is a list of rename and delete.
sub: trace add execution NAME OPS CMD | OPS is a list of enter, leave, enterstep, and leavestep.
sub: trace remove TYPE NAME OPS CMD | Removes a trace.
sub: trace info TYPE NAME | The traces of a name.
sub: trace variable NAME OPS CMD | The old form of trace add variable.
sub: trace vdelete NAME OPS CMD | The old form of trace remove variable.
sub: trace vinfo NAME | The old form of trace info variable.
== if
syn: if expr1 ?then? body1 elseif expr2 ?then? body2 ... ?else? ?bodyN?
== while
syn: while test command
== for
syn: for start test next command
== break
syn: break
== continue
syn: continue
== switch
syn: switch ?-option ...? string ?pattern body ...? ?default body?
opt: -exact | The pattern equals the string (the default).
opt: -glob | A glob pattern.
opt: -regexp | A regular expression.
opt: -integer | Tcl 9.1 only: the pattern and the string are the same integer, such as 16 and 0x10.
opt: -nocase | Matches letters with no case.
opt: -- | The end of the options, for a string that starts with -.
== case
syn: case string ?in? ?pattern body ...? ?default body?
== eval
syn: eval arg ?arg ...?
== uplevel
syn: uplevel ?level? command ?arg ...?

syn: apply lambdaExpr ?arg ...?
== time
syn: time command ?count?
== timerate
syn: timerate ?-direct? ?-calibrate? ?-overhead double? command ?time ?max-count??
== proc
syn: proc name args body
== return
syn: return ?-code code? ?-errorcode list? ?-level n? ?-options dict? ?value?
== tailcall
syn: tailcall command ?arg ...?
== rename
syn: rename oldName newName
== namespace
syn: namespace subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: namespace eval NS SCRIPT | Runs SCRIPT in NS, and makes NS when it does not exist.
sub: namespace current | The name of the current namespace.
sub: namespace children ?NS? ?PATTERN? | The namespaces in NS.
sub: namespace parent ?NS? | The namespace around NS.
sub: namespace exists NS | 1 when NS exists.
sub: namespace delete ?NS ...? | Removes namespaces with their commands and variables.
sub: namespace export ?-clear? ?PATTERN ...? | The commands that other code can import, and that an ensemble has.
sub: namespace import ?-force? ?PATTERN ...? | Makes the exported commands of another namespace callable by their short names.
sub: namespace forget ?PATTERN ...? | Removes imported commands.
sub: namespace ensemble create ?-option value ...? | Makes the namespace a command with its exported commands as subcommands.
sub: namespace path ?LIST? | The namespaces where a command name is looked up after the current one.
sub: namespace which ?-command? ?-variable? NAME | The full name of a command or variable, or an empty string.
sub: namespace origin CMD | The full name of the command that an imported command points to.
sub: namespace qualifiers NAME | The part of NAME before its last ::.
sub: namespace tail NAME | The part of NAME after its last ::.
sub: namespace code SCRIPT | A script that runs in the current namespace from each place, for a callback.
sub: namespace inscope NS SCRIPT ?ARG ...? | Runs SCRIPT in NS.
sub: namespace upvar NS OTHERVAR MYVAR ?OTHERVAR MYVAR ...? | Links local names to variables of NS.
sub: namespace unknown ?SCRIPT? | The handler of an unknown command in the namespace.

== chan
syn: chan SUBCOMMAND ?ARG ...?
sub: chan puts ?-nonewline? ?CHAN? STRING | Writes a string and a newline to a channel.
sub: chan gets CHAN ?VAR? | Reads one line from a channel.
sub: chan read ?-nonewline? CHAN | Reads the rest of a channel, or a count of characters.
sub: chan read CHAN COUNT | Reads the rest of a channel, or a count of characters.
sub: chan eof CHAN | Tests whether the last read reached the end of a channel.
sub: chan seek CHAN OFFSET ?ORIGIN? | Moves the place of the next read or write of a channel.
sub: chan tell CHAN | Gives the place of the next read or write of a channel.
sub: chan flush CHAN | Writes the buffered output of a channel.
sub: chan close CHAN ?DIRECTION? | Closes a channel, or one direction of it.
sub: chan names ?PATTERN? | Gives the names of the open channels.
sub: chan configure CHAN | Gives or sets the options of a channel.
sub: chan configure CHAN OPTION | Gives or sets the options of a channel.
sub: chan configure CHAN OPTION VALUE ?OPTION VALUE ...? | Gives or sets the options of a channel.
sub: chan copy IN OUT ?-size SIZE? ?-command SCRIPT? | Copies the data of one channel to another.
sub: chan pipe | Makes a pipe and gives its two channels.
sub: chan pending MODE CHAN | Gives the count of bytes that wait in a buffer of a channel.
sub: chan blocked CHAN | Tests whether the last read of a channel stopped for want of data.
sub: chan event CHAN EVENT ?SCRIPT? | Gives or sets the script that the event loop runs when a channel can be read or written.
== file
syn: file SUBCOMMAND ?ARG ...?
sub: file join NAME ?NAME ...? | Joins parts into one path.
sub: file split NAME | Gives the parts of a path as a list.
sub: file dirname NAME | Gives a path with no last part.
sub: file tail NAME | Gives the last part of a path.
sub: file extension NAME | Gives the extension of the last part of a path, with its dot.
sub: file rootname NAME | Gives a path with no extension.
sub: file pathtype NAME | Gives the kind of a path: absolute, relative, or volumerelative.
sub: file normalize NAME | Gives the full path with each .
sub: file nativename NAME | Gives a path in the form of the platform.
sub: file separator ?NAME? | Gives the separator of paths.
sub: file mkdir ?DIR ...? | Makes folders, with each missing parent folder.
sub: file exists NAME | Tests whether a file or a folder exists.
sub: file isfile NAME | Tests whether a path is a file.
sub: file isdirectory NAME | Tests whether a path is a folder.
sub: file readable NAME | Tests whether a file can be read.
sub: file writable NAME | Tests whether a file can be written.
sub: file executable NAME | Tests whether a file has a permission to run.
sub: file owned NAME | Tests whether a file exists and is of the user.
sub: file size NAME | Gives the size of a file in bytes.
sub: file type NAME | Gives the kind of an entry of the file system: file, directory, link, and others.
sub: file mtime NAME | Gives the time of the last change of a file, in seconds.
sub: file atime NAME | Gives the time of the last read of a file, in seconds.
sub: file stat NAME VAR | Puts the facts of a file in an array.
sub: file lstat NAME VAR | Puts the facts of a file in an array, for a link itself.
sub: file attributes NAME ?OPTION ?VALUE ...?? | Gives or sets the attributes of the platform of a file; not available in ztcl.
sub: file copy ?-force? ?--? SOURCE TARGET | Copies files and folders.
sub: file copy ?-force? ?--? SOURCE ?SOURCE ...? DIR | Copies files and folders.
sub: file rename ?-force? ?--? SOURCE TARGET | Moves or renames files and folders.
sub: file rename ?-force? ?--? SOURCE ?SOURCE ...? DIR | Moves or renames files and folders.
sub: file delete ?-force? ?--? ?NAME ...? | Removes files and folders.
sub: file link ?-symbolic|-hard? LINK ?TARGET? | Makes a link, or gives the target of a link; not available in ztcl.
sub: file readlink NAME | Gives the target of a symbolic link; not available in ztcl.
sub: file tempfile ?VAR? ?TEMPLATE? | Opens a new temporary file and gives its channel.
sub: file channels ?PATTERN? | Gives the names of the open channels.
sub: file system NAME | Gives the file system of a path.
sub: file volumes | Gives the volumes of the file system.
== open
syn: open fileName ?access? ?permissions?
== close
syn: close channelId ?direction?
== gets
syn: gets channelId ?varName?
== read
syn: read ?-nonewline? channelId ?numChars?
== puts
syn: puts ?-nonewline? ?channelId? string
== flush
syn: flush channelId
== eof
syn: eof channelId
== seek
syn: seek channelId offset ?origin?
== tell
syn: tell channelId
== fconfigure
syn: fconfigure channelId ?-option value ...?
opt: -mode baud,parity,data,stop | A serial port: the baud, the parity (n, o, e, m, or s), the data bits (5 to 8), and the stop bits (1 or 2), for example 115200,n,8,1.
opt: -handshake type | A serial port: none, rtscts, xonxoff, or dtrdsr (Windows only).
opt: -xchar {xon xoff} | A serial port: the two characters of xonxoff.
opt: -ttycontrol {signal value ...} | A serial port: sets the lines RTS, DTR, and BREAK, for example {DTR 0 RTS 1}.
opt: -ttystatus | A serial port, read only: a dict of the lines CTS, DSR, RING, and DCD.
opt: -queue | A serial port, read only: the counts of bytes in the input queue and the output queue of the system.
== fblocked
syn: fblocked channelId
== fcopy
syn: fcopy input output ?-size size? ?-command callback?
== source
syn: source ?-encoding name? fileName
== glob
syn: glob ?switches? name ?name ...?
opt: -nocomplain | No match gives an empty list.
opt: -directory DIR | Matches in DIR.
opt: -types TYPES | Only files of the types, such as f and d.
opt: -tails | Gives the names without the folder of -directory.
== cd
syn: cd ?dirName?
== pwd
syn: pwd
== zipfs
syn: zipfs subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: zipfs mount ?ZIPFILE? ?MOUNTPOINT? | Mounts a zip file, or gives the mounts.
sub: zipfs unmount MOUNTPOINT | Removes a mount.
sub: zipfs list ?(-glob|-regexp)? ?PATTERN? | The names of the files in the mounts.
sub: zipfs exists NAME | 1 when the file is in a mount.
sub: zipfs info NAME | The zip file, the size, the packed size, and the offset of a file.
sub: zipfs root | The root of the mounts: //zipfs:/.

== tcl::Bgerror bgerror
syn: tcl::Bgerror message options
== interp
syn: interp cmd ?arg ...?
sub: interp create ?-safe? ?-meter NAME? ?--? ?PATH? | A new child, and its path.
sub: interp eval PATH ARG ?ARG ...? | Runs a script in the child.
sub: interp alias SRCPATH SRCCMD TARGETPATH TARGETCMD ?ARG ...? | Makes SRCCMD of the child run TARGETCMD of the parent.
sub: interp aliases ?PATH? | The aliases of a child.
sub: interp delete ?PATH ...? | Removes children.
sub: interp exists PATH | 1 when the child exists.
sub: interp children ?PATH? | The children.
sub: interp cancel ?-unwind? ?--? ?PATH? ?RESULT? | Stops the script of the interp with the error "eval canceled", or RESULT.
sub: interp slaves ?PATH? | The old name of children.
sub: interp issafe ?PATH? | 1 for a safe interpreter.
sub: interp hide PATH CMD ?NAME? | Hides a command from the scripts of the child.

== thread thread::attach thread::broadcast thread::cancel thread::cond thread::configure thread::create thread::detach thread::errorproc thread::eval thread::exists thread::exit thread::id thread::join thread::mutex thread::names thread::preserve thread::release thread::rwmutex thread::send thread::transfer thread::unwind thread::wait

== info
syn: info subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: info commands ?PATTERN? | The names of the commands.
sub: info procs ?PATTERN? | The names of the procs.
sub: info exists VAR | 1 when the variable has a value.
sub: info vars ?PATTERN? | The visible variables.
sub: info globals ?PATTERN? | The variables of the top level.
sub: info locals ?PATTERN? | The local variables of the proc.
sub: info args PROC | The argument names of a proc.
sub: info body PROC | The body of a proc.
sub: info default PROC ARG VAR | 1 when the argument has a default, which goes in VAR.
sub: info level ?N? | The depth of the call stack, or the command at level N.
sub: info complete SCRIPT | 1 when the script has no open brace, bracket, or quote.
sub: info script ?NAME? | The file of the script that source runs.
sub: info functions ?PATTERN? | The names of the math functions.
sub: info cmdcount | The count of commands that ran.
sub: info patchlevel | The version of Tcl that ztcl follows: 9.1.0, or 8.6.16 with --tcl 8.6.
sub: info tclversion | 9.1, or 8.6 with --tcl 8.6.
sub: info library | The folder of the Tcl library: empty in ztcl.
sub: info loaded | The loaded binary packages.
sub: info nameofexecutable | The path of the program.
sub: info sharedlibextension | The extension of a shared library.
sub: info hostname | The name of the host.
sub: info errorstack ?INTERP? | The -errorstack of the last error: INNER and the failed command, then CALL and the words of each proc that the error left, and UP and a count of levels for a catch in the frame of uplevel.
sub: info coroutine | The full name of the running coroutine, or an empty string.
sub: info class SUBCOMMAND CLASS ?arg ...? | Facts about a TclOO class, as info class of Tcl 8.6.
sub: info object SUBCOMMAND OBJECT ?arg ...? | Facts about a TclOO object, as info object of Tcl 8.6.
